CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.error: Says talents come from luck or from oneself alone.

example.question: Where do talents and abilities come from?
example.correct_answer: From God

CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.cause: The child has heard people called "lucky" to be gifted.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.reveals: Offer "From luck" beside "From God" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.help: Read Exodus 31:3: God filled Bezalel with skill. Ask the child to name a gift and say who gave it.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.feedback: Exodus 31:3 says God gave Bezalel his skill. Talents are gifts from God.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.error: Says a talent is for showing off or for oneself only.

example.question: What are talents given for?
example.correct_answer: To serve others

CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.cause: Talent shows on TV reward the best performer, so a talent looks like a prize to display.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.reveals: Offer "To show off" beside "To serve others" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.help: Link 1 Peter 4:10 with Romans 12:4: each part of the body works for the whole. Ask how a singer serves the church.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.feedback: Romans 12:4 shows that each part of the body serves the whole. Talents are for serving others.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.error: Mixes what Exodus 31:3 and Romans 12:4 say.

example.question: Which verse says the body has many parts with different work?
example.correct_answer: Romans 12:4

CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.cause: Both verses are learnt in one lesson and the references blur.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.reveals: Offer "Exodus 31:3" beside "Romans 12:4" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.help: Give each verse a picture: Exodus 31:3, a craftsman; Romans 12:4, a body with many parts.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.feedback: Romans 12:4 compares us to one body with many parts. Exodus 31:3 is about God filling Bezalel with skill.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_TAL6.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_C6_T.error: Thinks only talents that earn marks or money count, so singing, kindness or craft are not talents.

example.question: Which of these is a God-given talent?
example.correct_answer: Any gift, such as singing, drawing, farming, kindness or leading

CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_C6_T.cause: School rewards marks most, so the child ranks other gifts lower.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_C6_T.reveals: Offer "Only being top in exams" beside "Any gift, such as singing, drawing, farming, kindness or leading" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_C6_T.help: List gifts in the class; Bezalel's gift was craftwork (Exodus 31:3). Every gift serves.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_C6_T.feedback: Talents are many: singing, drawing, crafts, kindness, leading. God gives them all to serve others.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE.TALENTS.M_C6_T.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.error: Says God made the woman from dust or from clay.

example.question: What did God use to make the woman (Genesis 2:21-22)?
example.correct_answer: A rib taken from the man

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.cause: The child knows the man was made from dust (Genesis 2:7) and gives the woman the same origin.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.reveals: Offer "The dust of the ground" beside "A rib taken from the man" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.help: Put Genesis 2:7 and 2:21-22 side by side: the man from dust, the woman from the man's rib.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.feedback: Genesis 2:21-22 says God took one of the man's ribs and made the woman.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.error: Says a man stays in his parents' home when he marries.

example.question: What does Genesis 2:24 say a man does when he marries?
example.correct_answer: He leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.cause: In many homes a son's family lives near his parents, so the child reads leaving as wrong.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.reveals: Offer "He stays with his parents" beside "He leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.help: Explain that "leave" means a new household and first loyalty to the spouse, while still honouring parents.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.feedback: Genesis 2:24 says a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.error: Mixes the details of the sleep and the rib.

example.question: What did God do before he took the rib?
example.correct_answer: He put the man into a deep sleep

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.cause: The child retells from memory and puts the events in the order of an operation he imagines.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.reveals: Offer "He woke the man" beside "He put the man into a deep sleep" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.help: Read 2:21 aloud and number the events: deep sleep, rib taken, flesh closed, woman made.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.feedback: Genesis 2:21 says God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.error: Thinks early marriage helps a girl or her family.

example.question: What is a result of early marriage for a girl?
example.correct_answer: She may leave school and face health risks

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.cause: The child has heard that marriage brings a girl security or the family dowry.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.reveals: Offer "She has a better future" beside "She may leave school and face health risks" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.help: List what a girl loses (school, health, choice) against what is promised; read the 18-year rule.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.feedback: Early marriage often ends school, brings early pregnancy and its risks, and deepens poverty.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.error: Says a person may marry at 14 in Kenya, taking a custom some have heard of as the law, instead of 18.

example.question: In Kenya at what age may a person marry?
example.correct_answer: 18 years

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.cause: Some communities have married girls young and the child takes custom as law.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.reveals: Offer "14 years" beside "18 years" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.help: Say clearly: in Kenya the law sets 18. Ask what the law protects.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.feedback: The law in Kenya says a person must be 18 to marry.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.error: Thinks a child at risk should keep quiet.

example.question: A girl is told she will be married next month. What should she do?
example.wrong_answer: Keep quiet to respect her elders
example.correct_answer: Tell a teacher, the chief or Childline 116

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.cause: Respect for elders is taught strongly, so speaking up feels like disobedience.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.reveals: Offer "Keep quiet to respect her elders" beside "Tell a teacher, the chief or Childline 116" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.help: Explain that telling a teacher or the chief is how a child stays safe and is not disrespect. Name Childline 116.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.feedback: A child at risk should tell a safe adult. Help is available, including Childline Kenya 116.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.error: Thinks God named the woman, when the man said "she shall be called woman" (Genesis 2:23).

example.question: Who said "she shall be called woman" (Genesis 2:23)?
example.correct_answer: The man

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.cause: God does most of the speaking in Genesis 1-2, so the child gives God this line too.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.reveals: Offer "God" beside "The man" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.help: Read 2:23 and ask who is speaking: "bone of my bones". It is the man.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.feedback: The man said, "This is now bone of my bones... she shall be called woman."
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.MARRI.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.error: Thinks early marriage is a problem only for girls and that a boy marrying young is fine.

example.question: Is early marriage harmful for boys too?
example.correct_answer: Yes: boys also leave school and take on burdens too early

CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.cause: Most stories the child hears are of girls married young.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.reveals: Offer "No, only for girls" beside "Yes: boys also leave school and take on burdens too early" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.help: List results for a boy: leaves school, must provide too early, poverty. The law is 18 for both.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.feedback: Early marriage harms boys too. The law says 18 for everyone.
CRES.G6.CREATI.MARRIAGE_AND_FAMILY.EARLY.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.error: Says God rested because he was tired.

example.question: Why did God rest on the seventh day (Genesis 2:2-3)?
example.correct_answer: He had finished his work, and he blessed the day and made it holy

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.cause: People rest when tired, so the child gives God the same reason.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.reveals: Offer "He was tired" beside "He had finished his work, and he blessed the day and made it holy" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.help: Read Genesis 2:2-3: God finished, blessed and made holy. Ask whether God gets tired (Isaiah 40:28).
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.feedback: Genesis 2:2-3 says God finished his work, rested, blessed the day and made it holy.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

example.question: What does 1 Timothy 5:13 warn against?
example.correct_answer: Idleness that leads to gossip and meddling

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.cause: The child hears "leisure" as free time with nothing in it.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.reveals: Offer "Resting at all" beside "Idleness that leads to gossip and meddling" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.help: Contrast rest that refreshes with idleness that leads to gossip (1 Timothy 5:13).
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.feedback: 1 Timothy 5:13 warns against idleness that leads to gossip and meddling. Rest itself is good.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.error: Says God rested on the sixth day, the day people were made, instead of the seventh.

example.question: On which day did God rest (Genesis 2:2)?
example.correct_answer: The seventh day

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.cause: The sixth day is when people were made, and the child joins the last thing made with the rest.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.reveals: Offer "The sixth day" beside "The seventh day" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.help: Count the days on the fingers: six of creating, the seventh of rest.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.feedback: Genesis 2:2 says God rested on the seventh day.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_LE.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.error: Thinks drugs, gambling or too much phone time are fine ways to use free time.

example.question: Which is a good use of free time?
example.correct_answer: Reading or helping at home

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.cause: Free time is time "for me", so the child thinks anything goes.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.reveals: Offer "Gambling with friends" beside "Reading or helping at home" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.help: Sort cards into builds up and pulls down, and name the harm of each misuse.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.feedback: Gambling, drugs and endless phone time waste time and can harm. Reading, sport and helping are good uses.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.error: Thinks free time has no limits or no value.

example.question: Which value helps a youth use leisure well?
example.correct_answer: Self-control

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.cause: The group decides what is fun, and the child follows it.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.reveals: Offer "Doing whatever pleases the group" beside "Self-control" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.help: Name values: self-control, responsibility, time management. Ask what each looks like on a Saturday.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.feedback: Self-control and responsibility help us use free time well.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_LEI.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_C6.error: Thinks God's rest means God stopped caring for the world after creation.

example.question: After God rested on the seventh day, did he stop caring for the world?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, he left the world alone
example.correct_answer: No: he finished creating, and he still cares for his world

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_C6.cause: The child pictures rest as switching off.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_C6.reveals: Offer "Yes, he left the world alone" beside "No: he finished creating, and he still cares for his world" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_C6.help: Read Psalm 121:4: he who watches over Israel will neither slumber nor sleep. God rested from creating, not from caring.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_C6.feedback: God rested from the work of creating. He never stops caring for his world.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_REST.M_C6.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.error: Thinks spending a whole holiday on a phone or TV is a good use of leisure because it is not harmful.

example.question: Halima spends every day of the holiday on her phone from morning to night. Is this good use of leisure?
example.correct_answer: No: it wastes time and crowds out rest, chores, family and reading

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.cause: Screen time is not named as a sin, so the child thinks it is fine in any amount.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.reveals: Offer "Yes, it is harmless" beside "No: it wastes time and crowds out rest, chores, family and reading" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.help: Draw a day as a pie: sleep, chores, family, play, reading, screen. What happens if screen fills it?
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.feedback: Phones are not bad, but a whole day on one crowds out rest, family and growing. Use leisure wisely.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.error: Thinks only play counts as leisure, not reading, hobbies, church activities or helping others.

example.question: Which of these is a good use of leisure?
example.correct_answer: Reading, a hobby, sport, visiting the sick or a church activity

CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.cause: The child knows leisure only as play time.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.reveals: Offer "Only playing games" beside "Reading, a hobby, sport, visiting the sick or a church activity" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.help: List leisure activities in four groups: rest, play, learn, serve. All can be good.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.feedback: Leisure can be play, but also reading, hobbies, sport and helping others.
CRES.G6.CREATI.LEISURE.LEISURE_USE.M_C6_.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.error: Says the Bible has one author.

example.question: How many authors does the Bible have?
example.wrong_answer: One person wrote all of it
example.correct_answer: Many people wrote it, inspired by God

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.cause: The Bible is one book with one cover, so the child expects one writer.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.reveals: Offer "One person wrote all of it" beside "Many people wrote it, inspired by God" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.help: Show the contents page: many books, written over many years by many writers, all inspired by God.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.feedback: Many people, such as Moses, David and Paul, wrote the books of the Bible as God inspired them.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.error: Thinks the Bible is only the ideas of wise men, missing that 2 Timothy 3:16 calls Scripture God-breathed.

example.question: What does 2 Timothy 3:16 say about Scripture?
example.wrong_answer: It is only the ideas of wise men
example.correct_answer: It is God-breathed

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.cause: The child knows people wrote the Bible and stops there.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.reveals: Offer "It is only the ideas of wise men" beside "It is God-breathed" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.help: Read 2 Timothy 3:16: "God-breathed". People wrote, God inspired.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.feedback: 2 Timothy 3:16 says all Scripture is God-breathed.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.error: Gives winning arguments or making money as a use of Scripture, instead of teaching, correcting and training in righteousness.

example.question: What is Scripture useful for (2 Timothy 3:16)?
example.correct_answer: Teaching, correcting and training in righteousness

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.cause: The child has seen verses quoted to win an argument.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.reveals: Offer "Winning arguments and making money" beside "Teaching, correcting and training in righteousness" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.help: Read 2 Timothy 3:16-17 and list its four uses: teaching, rebuking, correcting, training in righteousness.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.feedback: 2 Timothy 3:16 says Scripture is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.INSP.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

example.question: Does translating the Bible change its message?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, it makes a new message
example.correct_answer: No, it puts the same message into another language

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.cause: The child has seen poor translations or mistranslated signs.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.reveals: Offer "Yes, it makes a new message" beside "No, it puts the same message into another language" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.help: Show one verse in English, Kiswahili and a local language: same meaning, different words.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.feedback: Translators carry the same message into a new language so that more people can understand.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.error: Thinks there is no need to translate because English is enough for everyone.

example.question: Why translate the Bible into local languages?
example.wrong_answer: There is no need: English is enough for everyone
example.correct_answer: So people can understand it in their own language

CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.cause: The child has heard English treated as the "proper" language of church and school.
CRES.G6.THE_BI.INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD.TRAN.reveals: Offer "There is no need: English is enough for everyone" beside "So people can understand it in their own language" and ask the child to choose.

CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..error: Names being busy with school and sport as a cause of irresponsible behaviour, instead of peer pressure and too little guidance.

example.question: Which can lead a young person into irresponsible behaviour?
example.wrong_answer: Staying busy with school and sport
example.correct_answer: Peer pressure and too little guidance

CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..cause: The child does not yet see what leads young people astray.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..reveals: Offer "Staying busy with school and sport" beside "Peer pressure and too little guidance" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..help: List real causes: peer pressure, idleness, media, too little guidance, drugs. Busy with good things protects.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..feedback: Peer pressure, harmful content, idleness and too little guidance are causes.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..error: Thinks what films and music show about relationships is how everyone lives, so it must be right.

example.question: Films show young people in sexual relationships as normal. What does the Bible teach?
example.correct_answer: Keep sex for marriage and honour God with your body

CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..cause: Media are the loudest voice the child hears on this.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..reveals: Offer "It is normal and right" beside "Keep sex for marriage and honour God with your body" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..help: Contrast what a film shows with 1 Corinthians 6:18-20. Ask who made the film and why.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..feedback: Films do not decide what is right. God teaches us to keep sex for marriage and honour him with our bodies.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..error: Thinks a young person cannot refuse once someone older or popular insists.

example.question: Someone older insists you go alone with them to their house. Can you refuse?
example.wrong_answer: No, I must obey an older person
example.correct_answer: Yes: say no, go away and tell a trusted adult

CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..cause: Children are taught to obey elders and feel they have no right to refuse.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..reveals: Offer "No, I must obey an older person" beside "Yes: say no, go away and tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..help: Practise assertiveness: a child may always refuse what is wrong or unsafe, even from an adult.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY_7_LESSON..feedback: You can always say no to what is wrong or unsafe, even to an older person, and tell a trusted adult.

CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.error: Thinks a life is one's own to take or harm.

example.question: Where does life come from?
example.correct_answer: It is a gift from God

CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.cause: The child thinks what is mine is mine to use.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.reveals: Offer "From ourselves alone" beside "It is a gift from God" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.help: Read Genesis 2:7: God breathed life into the man. Life is a gift we care for.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.feedback: Life is a gift from God, so we protect it.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

example.question: A crowd catches a thief and wants to beat him. What is right?
example.correct_answer: Hand him to the police, since life must be protected

CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.cause: The child has seen crowds punish thieves and thinks it is justice.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.reveals: Offer "Join in, he deserves it" beside "Hand him to the police, since life must be protected" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.help: Ask: who has the right to judge? The police and courts. Every life, even a thief's, is sacred.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.feedback: Mob justice violates the right to life. Hand a suspect to the police.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.error: Thinks only physical killing matters, not hatred.

example.question: What does Jesus teach about anger (Matthew 5:21-22)?
example.correct_answer: Anger and hatred also harm and must be dealt with

CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.cause: The child thinks only acts count, not feelings.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.reveals: Offer "Anger is harmless" beside "Anger and hatred also harm and must be dealt with" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.help: Read Matthew 5:21-22: Jesus names anger and insults too. Deal with anger early.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.feedback: In Matthew 5:21-22 Jesus teaches that anger toward a brother is also serious.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.error: Thinks harming one's own body by drugs or reckless dares does not break the sanctity of life.

example.question: Does taking drugs or reckless dares go against the sacredness of life?
example.wrong_answer: No, it is only my own life
example.correct_answer: Yes: my life is God's gift too, so I protect it

CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.cause: The child thinks sanctity of life is only about not hurting others.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.reveals: Offer "No, it is only my own life" beside "Yes: my life is God's gift too, so I protect it" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.help: Read 1 Corinthians 6:19-20: your body is not your own. Protect your own life as well as others'.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.feedback: Your own life is God's gift too. Protect it, as you protect others'.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks all medicine is drug abuse.

example.question: Which is drug abuse?
example.wrong_answer: Taking medicine as the doctor directs
example.correct_answer: Sniffing glue

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The word drug is used for medicine and for abuse.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Taking medicine as the doctor directs" beside "Sniffing glue" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Sort cards: medicine as the doctor directs (use); glue, bhang, alcohol for a high (abuse).
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Medicine taken as a health worker directs is not abuse. Sniffing glue is.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

example.question: What is true of trying a harmful drug once?
example.correct_answer: It can start an addiction

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The child thinks harm comes only from many times.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "It is harmless" beside "It can start an addiction" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Explain addiction simply: the body asks for more. Many addicts began with "just once".
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Trying once can lead to addiction.

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks Ephesians 5:18 says "drink wine with joy", instead of "do not get drunk on wine, but be filled with the Spirit".

example.question: What does Ephesians 5:18 say?
example.correct_answer: Do not get drunk on wine, but be filled with the Spirit

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The child has seen wine at weddings in the Bible and thinks drinking is praised.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Drink wine with joy" beside "Do not get drunk on wine, but be filled with the Spirit" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Read Ephesians 5:18 and Hosea 4:11: do not get drunk; wine takes away understanding.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Ephesians 5:18 says do not get drunk, but be filled with the Spirit.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Names the examinations council instead of NACADA as the body that campaigns against drug abuse.

example.question: Which authority runs campaigns against alcohol and drug abuse?
example.correct_answer: NACADA

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The child knows national bodies like KNEC from school and picks one.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "The National Examinations Council" beside "NACADA" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Write NACADA in full: National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse. Add the police.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: NACADA is the National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks a person who abuses drugs should be hidden or abandoned.

example.question: A friend is addicted to drugs. What is the Christian response?
example.wrong_answer: Avoid him and tell no one
example.correct_answer: Support him and help him find a counsellor

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: Shame and fear make the child want to avoid an addicted friend.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Avoid him and tell no one" beside "Support him and help him find a counsellor" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Read Galatians 6:2: carry each other's burdens. Name counsellors, pastors and rehabilitation centres.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Christians care for those who struggle and help them get counselling and treatment.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks saying no is rude or weak.

example.question: A friend offers you cigarettes. What do you do?
example.wrong_answer: Accept so as not to look weak
example.correct_answer: Refuse firmly, walk away and tell an adult

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: Saying no feels unfriendly and risky.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Accept so as not to look weak" beside "Refuse firmly, walk away and tell an adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Practise three ways to say no and walk away. Strong people say no.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Saying no firmly takes courage. Walk away and tell an adult.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks getting drunk is wrong only for children and fine for adults.

example.question: According to Ephesians 5:18, is getting drunk right for adults?
example.correct_answer: No: the verse says do not get drunk, for everyone

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The child sees adults drinking and links the rule only with age.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Yes, adults may get drunk" beside "No: the verse says do not get drunk, for everyone" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Read Ephesians 5:18 aloud: it is written to all believers. Name the harm drunkenness does to families.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Ephesians 5:18 says do not get drunk. It is for adults too.

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks only the police can fight drug abuse, so ordinary Christians have no part.

example.question: Who can help fight drug abuse?
example.correct_answer: Families, churches, schools, NACADA, the police and young people themselves

CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: Arrests are what the child sees on the news.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Only the police" beside "Families, churches, schools, NACADA, the police and young people themselves" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Make a circle of helpers: family, church, school, NACADA, police, friends. Ask what each does.
CRES.G6.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Everyone has a part: families, churches, schools, NACADA, the police and you.
